Pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and the: Pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and the next morning's Fajr shortened (Qasr — 2 rak'ahs for 4-rak'ah prayers) on time, without combining.

The supreme day of the entire pilgrimage: The supreme day of the entire pilgrimage. The Prophet ﷺ declared: "Hajj is Arafah." Pilgrims stand before Allah with open hands and weeping eyes, begging for forgiveness and mercy until the sun sets, then proceed peacefully to Muzdalifah.
Move to the plains of Arafah after sunri: Move to the plains of Arafah after sunrise. Settle into the camps before solar noon (Zawal).

Spend from midday until sunset standing: Spend from midday until sunset standing or sitting facing the Qibla, raising hands continuously in supplication and repentance. Presence within Arafah boundaries is essential.
After the sun sets completely, leave Ara: After the sun sets completely, leave Arafah for Muzdalifah with calmness and composure without praying Maghrib at Arafah.
Upon arrival at Muzdalifah, combine Magh: Upon arrival at Muzdalifah, combine Maghrib (3) and Isha (shortened to 2) with one adhan and two iqamahs.

Pray Fajr at dawn in Muzdalifah, stand f: Pray Fajr at dawn in Muzdalifah, stand facing Qibla making dua until just before sunrise, then proceed to Mina.

After stoning the Small and Medium Jamar: After stoning the Small and Medium Jamarat, step to the side facing the Qibla and make long, heartfelt personal du'a.

For pilgrims who stay the 13th (Ta'akhkh: For pilgrims who stay the 13th (Ta'akhkhur), they stone the three Jamarat one last time after midday. Before leaving Makkah to return home, all pilgrims perform the Farewell Tawaf (Tawaf al-Wida') as their final act in the sacred city.
Stone all three pillars after Zawal (21: Stone all three pillars after Zawal (21 pebbles), gaining greater spiritual reward as mentioned in Quran (2:203).
Pack belongings and leave Mina permanent: Pack belongings and leave Mina permanently for Makkah.
Circumambulate the Kaaba 7 times immedia: Circumambulate the Kaaba 7 times immediately before departing Makkah. No Sa'i is required. Women in menses or postpartum bleeding are exempt.
O Allah, this is Your House and I am You: O Allah, this is Your House and I am Your servant. You carried me upon that which You subjected for me of Your creation, so do not let this be the last time I visit Your Sacred House.
Pack all bags and finalize hotel checkou: Pack all bags and finalize hotel checkout before Tawaf al-Wida' so you can depart directly to the airport or train station.
Pray for acceptance: \"Rabbana taqabbal: Pray for acceptance: "Rabbana taqabbal minna innaka Antas-Sami'ul-'Aleem."
Entering the sacred state of consecratio: Entering the sacred state of consecration (Ihram) before crossing the Miqat. It involves physical purification, donning the prescribed garments, formulating the sincere intention for Umrah, and reciting the Talbiyah.
Perform Ghusl (ritual bath) and trim nai: Perform Ghusl (ritual bath) and trim nails/mustache before entering Ihram.
Men wear two seamless white sheets (Izar: Men wear two seamless white sheets (Izar wrapped around waist, Rida draped over shoulders). Head must remain uncovered.
Women wear modest, loose regular clothin: Women wear modest, loose regular clothing of any color, leaving the face and hands uncovered (no niqab or gloves in Ihram).
Formulate the Niyyah (intention): \"Labb: Formulate the Niyyah (intention): "Labbayk Allahumma Umrah" (لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ عُمْرَةً).
Begin reciting the Talbiyah aloud (men): Begin reciting the Talbiyah aloud (men) or softly (women) continuously until seeing the Kaaba.
Here I am, O Allah, for an Umrah.
Crossing the Miqat without Ihram require: Crossing the Miqat without Ihram requires expiation (Dam - sacrificing a sheep in Makkah).
Prohibitions in Ihram: No perfume, no cu: Prohibitions in Ihram: No perfume, no cutting hair or nails, no marital intimacy, no hunting, no stitched clothing conforming to limbs for men.
Arriving at the Grand Mosque in Makkah w: Arriving at the Grand Mosque in Makkah with humility, awe, and reverence. Step in with the right foot and supplicate for Allah's infinite mercy.
Stop reciting the Talbiyah upon reaching: Stop reciting the Talbiyah upon reaching the Kaaba.
Enter the Mosque with the right foot fir: Enter the Mosque with the right foot first and say the standard mosque entrance dua.
When gazing upon the Kaaba for the first: When gazing upon the Kaaba for the first time, raise hands and make heartfelt du'a — this is a moment when supplications are answered.
O Allah, You are Peace and from You is p: O Allah, You are Peace and from You is peace, so greet us our Lord with peace. O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.
Circumambulating the Holy Kaaba seven co: Circumambulating the Holy Kaaba seven complete times in a state of ritual purity (Wudu), beginning and ending at the Black Stone (Hajar al-Aswad) with the Kaaba on your left.
Purity (Wudu) is an obligatory condition: Purity (Wudu) is an obligatory condition for Tawaf according to majority of scholars.
Men perform Idtiba' (اضطباع): Uncover th: Men perform Idtiba' (اضطباع): Uncover the right shoulder by passing the upper garment under the right armpit and draped over the left shoulder (for Tawaf only).
Start in line with the Black Stone (mark: Start in line with the Black Stone (marked by green light on the Haram wall). Point the right hand towards it and recite: "Bismillahi Allahu Akbar" (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ).
Men perform Ramal (رَمَل): A brisk walk: Men perform Ramal (رَمَل): A brisk walk with short quick paces during the first 3 circuits, followed by normal walking in the remaining 4 circuits.
Supplicate freely during circumambulatio: Supplicate freely during circumambulation; there are no fixed words except between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone.
Touch the Yemeni Corner (Rukn al-Yamani): Touch the Yemeni Corner (Rukn al-Yamani) with the right hand without kissing if accessible, otherwise pass without pointing.
After the 7th circuit: Cover both should: After the 7th circuit: Cover both shoulders (end Idtiba'). Pray 2 Rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim (or anywhere in the Haram), reciting Surah al-Kafirun in the 1st rak'ah and Surah al-Ikhlas in the 2nd.
Drink Zamzam water from the dispensers,: Drink Zamzam water from the dispensers, make du'a, and pour some over your head.
Our Lord, give us in this world [that wh: Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
Hijr Ismail (Al-Hateem): The semi-circul: Hijr Ismail (Al-Hateem): The semi-circular walled area is part of the interior Kaaba. Walking INSIDE it invalidates that circuit. You must walk OUTSIDE the wall.
Avoid pushing, shoving, or attempting to: Avoid pushing, shoving, or attempting to kiss the Black Stone if it causes harm to fellow worshippers.
Walking seven laps between the hillocks: Walking seven laps between the hillocks of Safa and Marwah, commemorating the devotion of Lady Hajar (peace be upon her) as she sought water for infant Ismail.
Approach Mount Safa. As you near it, rec: Approach Mount Safa. As you near it, recite the Quranic verse (2:158) and declare: "Abda'u bima bada'allahu bih" (I begin with that which Allah began with).
Ascend Safa, face the Kaaba, raise your: Ascend Safa, face the Kaaba, raise your hands, and recite the prophetic takbir and declaration of tawheed 3 times with personal du'a in between.
Walk towards Marwah. When reaching the g: Walk towards Marwah. When reaching the green fluorescent markers, men run at a brisk jog, while women maintain their normal walking pace.
Upon reaching Marwah, face the Kaaba and: Upon reaching Marwah, face the Kaaba and repeat the same remembrance and supplication as on Safa.
Lap count: Safa to Marwah is Lap 1; Marw: Lap count: Safa to Marwah is Lap 1; Marwah to Safa is Lap 2. Lap 7 concludes at Marwah.
Ritual purity (Wudu) is highly recommend: Ritual purity (Wudu) is highly recommended for Sa'i, but unlike Tawaf, it remains valid if broken.
Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. I begin with that which Allah began with. There is no deity except Allah alone without partner, His is the sovereignty and His is praise, and He has power over all things; He fulfilled His promise, granted victory to His servant, and defeated the confederates alone.
Shaving the head or trimming the hair to: Shaving the head or trimming the hair to conclude the Umrah and officially exit the state of Ihram. All prior restrictions are now fully lifted.
Men have two options: Halq (shaving head: Men have two options: Halq (shaving head completely) or Taqsir (trimming hair evenly from all sides). Halq is superior: the Prophet ﷺ prayed thrice for those who shave and once for those who trim.
If trimming (men), hair must be cut from: If trimming (men), hair must be cut from all areas of the head, not merely a single snip from one side.
Women perform Taqsir only: gather the ha: Women perform Taqsir only: gather the hair and trim the length of a fingertip (approx. 1 to 2 cm) from the ends. Shaving is prohibited for women.
Upon completion of Halq or Taqsir, your: Upon completion of Halq or Taqsir, your Umrah is complete (Al-Tahallul) and all ordinary clothing and activities become lawful again.
Use licensed, hygienic barber shops loca: Use licensed, hygienic barber shops located across the clock tower and hotels surrounding the Haram that use sterilized single-use blades.
Do not exit Ihram or wear regular clothe: Do not exit Ihram or wear regular clothes until hair has been shaved or trimmed.

The Hateem is part of the interior Kaaba: The Hateem is part of the interior Kaaba. You must circumambulate OUTSIDE the curved wall, otherwise the circuit is invalid.
Leaving the right shoulder uncovered thr: Leaving the right shoulder uncovered throughout the entire trip, including during Salah and Sa'i.
Idtiba' (uncovering the right shoulder): Idtiba' (uncovering the right shoulder) is Sunnah ONLY during the 7 circuits of Tawaf. Cover both shoulders before praying 2 rak'ahs and during Sa'i.
Rubbing the cloth of the Kaaba (Kiswah),: Rubbing the cloth of the Kaaba (Kiswah), the door, or the walls believing they transmit barakah.

Snipping a tiny lock of hair from one si: Snipping a tiny lock of hair from one side of the head with small scissors and declaring Umrah complete.
For men, hair must be shortened evenly a: For men, hair must be shortened evenly across the ENTIRE head. For women, trim the length of a fingertip (1–2 cm) from all hair ends.
Pushing, jostling, or aggressively forci: Pushing, jostling, or aggressively forcing a path towards the Black Stone or Maqam Ibrahim.
Preserving the physical safety and tranq: Preserving the physical safety and tranquility of fellow believers is an obligation (Wajib), whereas kissing the Stone is Sunnah. Prioritize safety.
Holding phones aloft to livestream or re: Holding phones aloft to livestream or record oneself during Tawaf, distracting oneself and other worshippers.
Maintain presence of heart and reverence: Maintain presence of heart and reverence. Focus on du'a, istighfar, and reflection rather than social media updates.

It was narrated from 'Aishah that she sa: It was narrated from 'Aishah that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think I should say in my supplication, if I come upon Laylatul-Qadr?" Malik related to me from Ibn Shihab from: Malik related to me from Ibn Shihab from Urwa ibn az-Zubayr that Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abd al-Qari said, "I went out with Umar ibn alKhattab in Ramadan to the mosque and the people there were spread out in groups. It was narrated from Abu Bishr Ja'far bi: It was narrated from Abu Bishr Ja'far bin Abi Wahshiyyah that: He heard Humaid bin 'Abdur-Rahman say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The best prayer after the obligatory (fard) prayers is prayer at night and the best fasting after the month of Ramadan is Al-Muharram.'" The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to do itikaf in the middle ten days of Ramadan.

Narrated `Aisha: (the wife of the Prophe: Narrated `Aisha: (the wife of the Prophet) Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to let his head in (the house) while he was in the mosque and I would comb and oil his hair. When in I`tikaf he used not to enter the house except for a need.
Narrated Ibn `Umar: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ: Narrated Ibn `Umar: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) enjoined the payment of one Sa' of dates or one Sa' of barley as Zakat-ul-Fitr on every Muslim slave or free, male or female, young or old, and he ordered that it be paid before the people went out to offer the `Id prayer. Narrated Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri: We used to: Narrated Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri: We used to give one Sa' of meal or one Sa' of barley or one Sa' of dates, or one Sa' of cottage cheese or one Sa' of Raisins (dried grapes) as Zakat-ul-Fitr.
The Prophet (ﷺ) used to proceed to the M: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to proceed to the Musalla on the days of Id-ul-Fitr and Id-ul-Adha; the first thing to begin with was the prayer and after that he would stand in front of the people and the people would keep sitting in their rows. ‘Abdur-Rahman bin Sa’d bin ‘Ammar bin Sa: ‘Abdur-Rahman bin Sa’d bin ‘Ammar bin Sa’d, the Mu’adhdhin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), narrated from his father, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say the Takbir in the ‘Eid prayer, seven times in the first (Rak’ah) before reciting Qur’an, and five times in the second before reciting Qur’an.
An-Numan bin Bashir narrated: \"For the: An-Numan bin Bashir narrated: "For the two Eid and the Friday prayer, the Prophet (ﷺ) would recite: Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High, and Has there come to you the narration of the overwhelming?
